outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to FeatLLM and the State of Tabular Learning
outline.description: This chapter establishes the foundational context for why Large Language Models (LLMs) are being explored for tabular data. It defines the specific challenges of few-shot learning in tabular domains, reviews current limitations of direct LLM-inference approaches (computational cost, prompt limits), and introduces the core philosophy of FeatLLM: shifting the LLM's role from end-to-end predictor to automated feature engineer.
subtopics: The rise of LLMs in reasoning and their potential for non-textual data.
Challenges in Few-Shot Tabular Learning: Spurious correlations and lack of priors.
Limitations of existing LLM-based tabular methods (Latency, Fine-tuning requirements, Context Window limits).
Core Thesis: Using LLMs for Feature Engineering rather than End-to-End Prediction.
Overview of the FeatLLM architecture: Rule generation -> Binary transformation -> Simple downstream modeling.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Related Work and Methodological Evolution
outline.description: Students will explore the history of few-shot learning algorithms tailored for tabular data and trace the evolution toward integrating linguistic models. This section critically analyzes why hybrid approaches (like Semantically Augmented Pre-training or Transfer Learning) fall short compared to generative rule-extraction, setting the stage for FeatLLM's unique contribution.
subtopics: Traditional Few-Shot Techniques: Semi-supervised learning, Contrastive Learning, and Unsupervised Pre-training pitfalls in tabular heterogeneity.
Transfer Learning Approaches: Column semantics (TransTab) vs. Synthetic Distribution mixing (TabPFN).
Language-Integrated Tabular Methods: Serializing data into text for LLM ingestion.
Direct Inference vs. Knowledge Distillation: Why querying every sample is inefficient.
The Gap: Moving from Black-Box Inference to White-Box Rule Extraction.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Formulation and Prompt Architecture for Rule Extraction
outline.description: A deep dive into the mechanics of prompting FeatLLM. Students will learn how to construct prompts that elicit high-quality decision rules from an LLM by mimicking human expert reasoning. This covers the three critical prompt components and the logic behind separating global knowledge from local evidence.
subtopics: Mathematical Formalization of K-Shots Tabular Classification Problems.
Prompt Component I: Basic Information Description (Task framing, Feature serialization).
Prompt Component II: Reasoning Instruction (Chain-of-Thought separation into Global Causality vs. Local Evidence).
Prompt Component III: Response Formatting Constraints for Programmatic Parsing.
Strategies for Managing Constraint Limits (Fixing rule counts, Type-aware rule generation).

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: From Natural Language Rules to Executable Features
outline.description: This technical chapter bridges symbolic AI with statistical learning. It details the pipeline for converting ambiguous natural language outputs from an LLM into deterministic binary features ready for machine learning models, addressing noise handling via meta-programming techniques.
subtopics: The Challenge of Parsing Noisy Text Outputs from Generative Models.
Meta-Promoting Code Generation: Leveraging LLMs to write executable Python functions from rules.
Handling Syntactic Variance (e.g., "greater than" vs ">") via Semantic Parsing.

Transforming Samples: Creating binary indicator vectors ($\mathbb{Z} \in \{0,1\}^R$).

Executing Parsed Logic safely in production environments.

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 5: Downstream Modeling and Ensemble Strategies
outline.description: With features engineered by the LLM covered, this chapter explains how a lightweight linear model learns to weigh these rules. Crucially, it explores how ensemble methods (Bagging + Stochastic Sampling) overcome individual rule errors and scale beyond token limit restrictions.
subtopics:
The Linear Classifier Objective Function with Non-Negative Weight Constraints.
Learning Importance Scores ($W_k$): Optimizing Cross-Entropy Loss on Few-Shot Data.
Why Softmax Projection Ensures Monotonic Contribution of Features.
The Power of Ensembling:
To Mitigate False Positives/Negatives in Individual Rule Sets.
Feature Bagging Strategy:
Managing Context Windows by sampling subsets of rows/columns.
Randomization Techniques:
Cultivating Diversity through Temperature scaling and Sample ordering shuffling.
Combining Probabilistic Predictions Across Multiple Trials.
